title: A Semester for the Group Chat
premise: Wendell Oyelaran has spent her whole life kneading other people's feelings into bread and keeping her own locked in the pantry, so when her best friend Priya vanishes leaving only a ring of keys to places Wendell has never seen, she follows them into a hidden network of students who trade secrets, favors, and small magics across their school. The keys mark Wendell as Priya's heir to the Ledger, an inheritance that grants power over the network but demands a price paid in memory — and the previous heirs all ended up hollow. To find Priya before the Ledger consumes what's left of her, Wendell must win both the baking championship she never wanted and the trust war inside the network, learning that power shared is the only kind that doesn't rot. In the end she breaks the Ledger open, gives its power back to everyone it was taken from, and brings Priya home half-remembered but whole enough to start again.
about_author: Tamsin Whitlock grew up above her grandmother's bakery in coastal Maine, where she learned that every recipe is a confession waiting to happen. She writes stories about stubborn kids, inherited burdens, and the families we assemble from scratch.

chapters.title: The Crumb Test
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Opening at 4 a.m. in the family bakery, Wendell bakes a grief loaf for a customer who can't cry, establishing her gift for baking feelings into bread. Beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At school, Wendell deflects Priya's push to enter the regional baking championship, revealing how thoroughly she's trained herself to want nothing loudly. Beat: the cost of self-erasure.

chapters.title: Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Priya misses their standing Friday dinner; by Saturday, police are at her house and seven unlabeled brass keys sit on Wendell's windowsill with a note: 'Don't tell them you have these.' Beat: dread blooming.

chapters.title: What the Police Don't Ask
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Interrogated gently by a detective who seems oddly unsurprised, Wendell lies badly about the keys and realizes adults already know more than they're saying. Beat: paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: The First Door
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The first key opens a maintenance closet behind the gym that opens onto a room full of letters, ledgers, and jars of preserved memories. Beat: wonder curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Network
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She's caught by Marcus, a senior archivist, who explains the Ledger: a student-run exchange of secrets and small magics operating beneath the school for decades. Beat: vertigo of hidden worlds.

chapters.title: Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus reports Wendell to the network's council, arguing she should be turned away; instead the aging Ledger-keeper, Odile, names Wendell Priya's heir. Beat: being claimed without consent.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Odile shows Wendell the memory-jars of former heirs — brilliant students now blank-eyed and gentle — and calls it 'a fair tuition.' Beat: horror dressed as tradition.

chapters.title: Flour and Alibi
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell keeps baking championship qualifiers while secretly mapping the keys' locations, lying to her parents for the first time. Beat: guilt as a rising dough.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A key opens the public library's sub-basement where debts are recorded; Wendell finds Priya's name written beside Odile's, dated the week she vanished. Beat: betrayal hypothesis forms.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wendell recruits Marcus and skeptical junior archivist Noor, each hiding their own stake in finding Priya. Beat: found family's first fragile stitch.

chapters.title: Quarterfinals
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell bakes a technically perfect loaf that tastes like nothing and loses points for it; a rival baker, Sana, clocks her distraction. Beat: the championship starts mattering against her will.

chapters.title: What Priya Wanted
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor reveals Priya had been investigating the fate of the hollowed heirs and believed the Ledger could be rewritten from inside. Beat: mission sharpens from rescue to reform.

chapters.title: The Third Key
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The key opens the boathouse where Odile first took the Ledger decades ago; Wendell experiences a flash of someone else's memory — Odile's own first day. Beat: inheritance as haunting.

chapters.title: Sana Sees
chapters.summary: Sana's POV. Sana confronts Wendell after catching her sneaking through the school at night; instead of exposing her, she offers help, having lost a brother to the network years ago. Beat: unexpected kinship.

chapters.title: Council of Ashes
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The council summons Wendell, tests her loyalty with a moral trap, and she passes by refusing to choose — earning Odile's cold respect. Beat: power noticing her.

chapters.title: Semifinals
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Baking her mother's heartbreak recipe, Wendell advances to finals and realizes the crowd can taste truth. Beat: her gift becomes a weapon she didn't ask for.

chapters.title: Memory on Consignment
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus confesses he pawned memories of his sister to pay a debt, and Wendell promises to buy them back. Beat: the price made personal.

chapters.title: The Fourth Key
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The key opens Priya's hidden dorm room, untouched, walls covered in the Ledger's history — including proof Odile was once an heir herself who survived by feeding others. Beat: villain's origin revealed.

chapters.title: Odile Offers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Odile offers Wendell the full inheritance early: take it now, save Priya, pay later. Wendell stalls, terrified she'll say yes. Beat: temptation with a gentle voice.

chapters.title: Halfway Hollow
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell finds a trace of Priya alive inside a memory-jar, conscious, fading. Time limit established: the jar seals permanently at solstice. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor wants to raid the vault immediately; Wendell insists on the slower legal path through the council. The alliance cracks. Beat: good people, wrong methods.

chapters.title: The Fifth Key
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The key opens the chapel attic where the original Ledger contract is kept — and Wendell reads the clause no one survives knowing: the keeper must be fed willingly. Beat: the trap's true shape.

chapters.title: Bread for the Enemy
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell bakes for Odile deliberately, reading her grief in the crumb: Odile was a foundling the network saved, then enslaved. Beat: enemy humanized, not excused.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The team reconciles and plans a two-front assault: Wendell competes in the championship final while the others breach the vault during the ceremony's cover. Beat: unity forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Finals
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell bakes a loaf containing everything she's been — fear, love, hope — and wins the championship that doesn't matter, crying in front of everyone. Beat: the careful girl undone by her own hands.

chapters.title: The Vault
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. During the ceremony, Marcus and Noor breach the vault but trip a ward that alerts Odile mid-victory. Beat: plan collapsing beautifully.

chapters.title: Confrontation
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell arrives at the vault; Odile offers one last deal — Priya's freedom for Wendell's memories. Wendell says yes. Beat: sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: What Wendell Forgot
chapters.summary: Priya's POV (inside the jar). Priya feels Wendell's memories pouring past her like light and fights to hold onto one thread of her friend's name. Beat: love persisting through erasure.

chapters.title: The Loophole
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor remembers the contract clause: the keeper must be fed willingly — so Wendell's willing sacrifice means Wendell is now the Ledger's keeper, not its meal. Beat: reversal.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Half-remembering herself, Wendell stands in the vault holding absolute power over the network — and finds she doesn't want it. Beat: power offered, refused.

chapters.title: Breaking the Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell shatters the master jar, releasing every stored memory back to its owner across the school in a single night. Beat: restitution as climax.

chapters.title: Odile Unmade
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flooded with her own returned memories, Odile collapses into the frightened foundling she was; Wendell chooses mercy over punishment. Beat: cycle acknowledged, broken.

chapters.title: Coming Home
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Priya wakes in the hospital missing chunks but gripping Wendell's hand; the detective closes the case with suspicious grace. Beat: rescue completed, scars visible.

chapters.title: Relearning
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell rebuilds her own memories from friends' stories, discovering they kept meticulous notes because they loved her. Beat: found family as archive.

chapters.title: The Empty Vault
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The network debates its future without the Ledger; Marcus retrieves his sister's memories and weeps in the sub-basement. Beat: grief and repair.

chapters.title: New Recipes
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Back in the bakery, Wendell teaches Priya and Sana to bake feelings into bread, passing on the gift freely instead of hoarding it. Beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: The Championship That Mattered
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The five friends hold their own tiny contest in the bakery kitchen; nobody wins and everybody does. Beat: joy earned plainly.

chapters.title: Keys Returned
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell mails the six remaining keys to the doors they opened, keeping only the first — the closet that started everything. Beat: letting go with intention.

chapters.title: A Semester for the Group Chat
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV via group chat messages. One year later, the friends text across distances; Priya sends a photo of bread shaped like a key, captioned 'still ours.' Beat: warmth, continuity, home.
